declarations.name: atomState
declarations.description:
A reactive field backed by an atom. Reads and writes look like a plain field; the element
re-renders when the value changes.

With no argument the atom is created per instance, so each element has its own. Passing an atom
binds the field to that one instead, which is how several elements follow one value:

  const name = createAtom("Ada");
  class NameField extends AcmeElement {
    `@atomState`(name) private name!: string;   // every instance reads and writes the same atom
  }

`compare` sets the equality the atom uses to decide whether anything changed. It defaults to
identity, so an object mutated in place does not re-render; pass `shallow` from the store package
for a field that holds an object it rebuilds.

findings: Analyzer 0.11.0 CLI ran under Bun with noWrite:true and a scratch config explicitly setting packagejson:false; no analyzer output was written into the repository.

Raw output for 330 modules has 321 module references not matching declared module paths. Three of those are external packages misclassified as local modules by double-quote handling. This is not 321 broken runtime imports.

Temporary correction of isBareModuleSpecifier quote removal repairs the three external named exports; published-path normalization through installed TypeScript resolution then maps all 1072 local references with no dangling targets.
The fixture uses .js source imports; TypeScript resolves them to .ts source for analysis. The house does not need to adopt .ts imports simply to satisfy the initial browser manifest experiment.

Path output mapping follows current src-to-dist build rules, not an approved future package layout. Only the four-module fixture's emitted file existence was checked; the complete project was not built.

Strict TypeScript 5.9.3 declaration emission and positive/negative public consumer checks pass for the two-field candidate and copied unchanged atomState. Fields retain string|undefined; manifest inheritance/attribute links work without custom decorator analysis.
Installed Lit compiler 1.1.2 compiles the fixture templates. All three engines preserve the expected 9/13 baseline, 8/8 object and 15/15 capture results with compiled output; no page errors.
CEM @internal hides helper members in that manifest but the current declaration build still exposes annotated public helpers in .d.ts. Final internal/public type visibility remains to resolve.

findings: Original capture candidate fails four of five ordinary-binding assertions in each engine when overlapping inputs are initially undefined or mix a literal attribute with a property binding.
Keeping first-seen positions even for undefined values fixes the three late-value assertions. This is a bounded alternative; its complete removal/other-path behaviour has not been retested.
The literal-attribute/property-binding case still fails: .paddingInline=${'8px'} before literal padding='16px' yields 8px inline instead of the declaration-order requirement's 16px.

A public ElementPart directive receiving the complete style input object passes all six targeted helper assertions per engine, retaining element identity and canonical input access. No private Lit API is used.
The helper is unapproved. Its prototype supports two already-defined string properties only; early definition, complete cleanup, responsive values and other paths remain to test.

Do not infer a complete declaration order from setter arrival or claim it is impossible through every API. If preserving the selected order requires a new Lit authoring helper, Peter decides that API trade-off.

nextDecision.status: Open; no user selection this turn
nextDecision.recommendation: Evaluate a complete-input Lit helper as the companion to the React wrapper, retaining individual component properties and the already-selected declaration-order semantics.
nextDecision.alternative: Revisit fixed overlap priority if avoiding a Lit authoring helper is more important; this would revise the prior declaration-order choice and must not be done silently.
nextDecision.otherNarrowerRoute: Consistent ordinary property bindings plus preserved undefined positions fix the tested late-value cases, but do not solve mixed literal-attribute/binding order; any restriction requires explicit scope and further verification.
